With over 100 enterprise SaaS connectors, flexible LLM choice, and robust APIs, Glean gives organizations the infrastructure to govern, scale, and customize AI across their entire business - without vendor lock-in or costly implementation cycles.

At its core, Glean is redefining how enterprises find, use, and act on knowledge. Its Enterprise Graph and Personal Knowledge Graph map the relationships between people, content, and activity, delivering deeply personalized, context-aware responses for every employee. This foundation powers Glean’s agentic capabilities - AI agents that automate real work across teams by accessing the industry’s broadest range of data: enterprise and world, structured and unstructured, historical and real-time. The result: measurable business impact through faster onboarding, hours of productivity gained each week, and smarter, safer decisions at every level.

Recognized by Fast Company as one of the World’s Most Innovative Companies (Top 10, 2025), by CNBC’s Disruptor 50, Bloomberg’s AI Startups to Watch (2026), Forbes AI 50, and Gartner’s Tech Innovators in Agentic AI, Glean continues to accelerate its global impact. If you’re excited to shape how the world works, you’ll help build systems used daily across Microsoft Teams, Zoom, ServiceNow, Zendesk, GitHub, and many more. You'll be deeply embedded where people get things done. You'll ship agentic capabilities on an open, extensible stack, with the craft and care required for enterprise trust, as we bring Work AI to every employee, in every company.

Glean is seeking a few Machine Learning engineers who want to focus on a combination of Quality and traditional ML work to help us build the Enterprise Brain. The Enterprise Brain team is developing a suite of proactive AI products that aims to revolutionize enterprise workflows by proactively detecting and automating tasks for users - thus unlocking true productivity. This is built on top of a deep user understanding and state of the art Enterprise graph. The project involves using both LLM and other advanced ML techniques, agent orchestration and cutting-edge ranking techniques.

* Work on deeply challenging ML problems involving user understanding and task prediction.
* Invent new LLM workflows and signals to improve reasoning, planning, and personalization.
* Design and optimize reinforcement learning and fine-tuning approaches to improve the quality of understanding, prediction and other agentic systems.
* Lead development of scalable evaluation, benchmarking, and optimization loops.
* Build and maintain robust ML pipelines for enterprise and knowledge graph construction.
* Drive initiatives to measure, monitor, and improve data quality, model quality, and end-to-end system performance.
* Collaborate with cross-functional teams to deeply understand customer pain points and deliver high-quality, production-ready ML solutions.
* Mentor junior engineers or learn from experienced ones in a tight-knit, high-velocity environment.

**About you:**

* You bring 6+ years of industry experience in machine learning engineering.
* You hold a BA/BS in computer science, math, sciences, or a related field.
* You have a proven ability to design, build, and ship production-ready models and systems.
* You bring demonstrated expertise in ML evaluation, benchmarking, and data quality.
* You are proficient in an ML framework of your choice, such as TensorFlow or PyTorch.
* You thrive in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment, turning open-ended customer and ML problems into clear priorities and production-ready solutions.
* You balance speed with quality, making pragmatic tradeoffs to deliver measurable progress without losing sight of production readiness.

**Location:**

* This role is hybrid (4 days a week in our Mountain View office)

The standard base salary range for this position is $200,000 - $280,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits.

The Solutions Architecture team sits within Marvell's Platform organization, which turns advanced silicon into deployable, customer-ready AI and cloud infrastructure. This team — the AI Solutions Lab — owns the validation layer that proves our platforms perform as promised, across compute, networking, and memory fabrics. Without it, Marvell could design great silicon but could never prove, at rack scale, that it performs the way customers expect — and hyperscalers don't buy chips on paper, they buy validated systems.  
  
Day to day, the team runs AI benchmarking experiments that mirror real customer workloads, operates GPU/HPC lab clusters, validates Marvell's Teralynx switching and AI fabrics under production-like conditions, and builds live demos for trade shows — carrying platform programs from concept to production.  
  
What sets this team apart is breadth of ownership: engineers here aren't limited to validating a single switch chip — they work across the full breadth of Marvell's AI platform portfolio, from Teralynx network fabrics to integrated optical platforms like co-packaged optics (CPO) and near-packaged optics (NPO), as well as emerging memory fabric products such as CXL and photonic fabric memory appliances. This cross-domain ownership — networking, optics, and memory, together — is work that's often siloed across separate teams elsewhere, and the results feed directly into customer proof points and executive reviews.

**What You Can Expect**

The NRE/SRE Engineer owns the compute and software foundation of the AI Solutions Lab. * Improve repeatability and operational efficiency through automation, infrastructure, code, and standardized workflows.
* Support cross-functional validation efforts and help convert lab output into reusable internal and external assets.

**Education and Certifications**

* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field; a PhD is a plus.
* Linux certifications, CKA certification, or similar Kubernetes certifications are preferred.

**Required Qualifications**

* MS in Electrical/Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field; 6+ years of experience as a software/systems engineer, with at least 4+ years of Linux/infrastructure experience.
* Strong Linux systems experience at scale, including solid data center and cluster operations fundamentals; development experience across both Windows and Linux environments.
* Proficient in Python/TCL scripting and automation, with familiarity in C/C++ API development; proficiency in Python specifically for metrics, observability, and pipeline automation.
* Experience with automation tools such as Ansible and Terraform.
* Experience building and maintaining test harnesses, workload libraries, test plans, result pipelines, and dashboards to support repeatable validation.
* Experience establishing baseline observability for cluster/system health, job execution, failures, utilization, and regression tracking.
* Hands-on experience with workload scheduling and orchestration (Kubernetes and/or Slurm) in a lab or production environment.

* Excellent interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills; customer-facing experience required.
* Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced lab environment

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience operating AI or HPC clusters in a lab or production environment.
* Working familiarity with a distributed training framework (PyTorch DDP/FSDP, NeMo, or similar) sufficient to interpret job failures, not just infrastructure symptoms.

jobs.description:
Creeda is an AI-powered franchise accounting platform. We sell live financial visibility to franchises so they can run their businesses better, and automation to franchise-focused bookkeeping firms so they can reduce costs and increase efficiency.

There are 850,000 franchises in the US, constituting a $921B industry. Creeda is growing very fast, so we are looking for the brightest engineers to help us execute.

**The role**

You'll start by building. We need a strong generalist who can work anywhere in the stack, front end to back end to data, and make the platform better wherever it needs it most. Some weeks that's shipping a feature a customer is waiting on, some weeks it's fixing an integration that breaks a bookkeeper's close, some weeks it's making onboarding faster so a firm can bring over hundreds of locations instead of fifty. You take a problem and own it end to end.

As we sign larger firms, the job will become more of a FDE role. You'll fly out, sit with their accountants, watch how they actually work, and build automations on site that go straight into production. Their bookkeepers describe what they need, you build it that week, and every firm serving that brand gets it. Half engineer, half the person our customers call when they want something built.

This is one of the highest-leverage seats at Creeda. You'll see the customer, write the code, and ship the fix in the same day.

Who this is not for

* Engineers who want clean specs and a well-defined surface. There is no such thing here yet.
* Engineers who do not want to talk to customers. Roughly a third of this job is people.
* Engineers who want to work only on the interesting parts. The data cleaning is not a phase we are going to grow out of; it is the product.

What we are looking forRequired

* Strong backend engineering in TypeScript or Python. We run both (TypeScript on Node and Next.js for the product, workers and importers; Python for the classifier and ML training) on Postgres. You need to be strong in one and willing to work in the other.
* Real experience with data that was not made for you: documents meant for humans (PDFs, spreadsheets a bookkeeper has already edited), vendor exports, third-party APIs that contradict themselves.
* Enough rigor to work on financial data, where being approximately right is being wrong. You should be able to explain why a balance check passing proves the arithmetic and not the entry.
* Judgment about code\*\*.\*\* We build with AI coding agents, and they are fast enough that the bottleneck has moved to review. You need software design fundamentals strong enough to look at generated code and say precisely why it is wrong. You should be good at the other end of it too, setting constraints up front so the agent produces something reviewable in the first place.
* Clear written communication. Every area of the codebase carries its own orientation doc, read by the next engineer and by the AI coding agents we build with, and we treat that documentation as an asset.
* Willingness to travel periodically once phase two begins, several multi-day trips per quarter

Helpful, not required

* Putting ML or LLM output into production behind hard constraints, where the model is allowed to be wrong but the system is not
* Double-entry bookkeeping. You know what a journal entry is and why it has to balance.
* Accounting, fintech, POS, payroll or ERP background
* QuickBooks Online's API, Plaid, or any general ledger system
* Having worked somewhere small enough that titles did not decide who did what

We do not require a CS degree, and we do not care where you worked before. We care that you have built something that had to be right.

Details

* **Location:** New York City
* **Visa:** We can accept CPT/OPT but unfortunately cannot sponsor H1B

Pay: $100,000.00 - $140,000.00 per year

Benefits:

* Dental insurance
* Health insurance

* Vision insurance
